_readme: Rules for .github/workflows/seo-automerge.yml, read from the default branch only. Third rework (2026-11-15): auto-merge only shapes that are easy to prove safe; everything else waits for Arsany. A pull request from a fix/seo-* or blog/* branch merges on its own when every Vercel status on its commit is green, every changed file matches allow (case-sensitive) and no deny (any case), the size limits hold, and every line passes. Built in, whatever this file says: workflows, package and lock files, config, env, middleware, routes, API, robots, scripts, HTML, public JS and JSON-LD files never merge; a changed line over 2,000 characters holds; deny checks test each line raw and folded (entities, %xx, every backslash escape form, invisible characters, accents and look-alike letters undone). fix branches: only existing .md, .mdx, .astro, .tsx and .jsx files (and .ts files named in metaObjects) can merge, and only when each change block removes and adds the same number of lines and every pair is one of these shapes: (1) a title, description, seoTitle or h1 value reworded in place: a frontmatter key, a key of export const metadata (or its openGraph or twitter block, or a metaObjects parent chain), its value on the next line, an .astro const, or a title or description attribute of an .astro <Base> tag before any expression on that line, with the rest of the line unchanged; (2) in Markdown, internal links added inside an existing sentence (a path starting with one /, no dot segments, % or backslash, no protected path), and on standard sites a reworded ## or ### heading; (3) on standard sites a one-line <h1> to <h6> element whose text is reworded, tag and attributes unchanged; (4) on standard sites a plain alt="..." on an image tag (img, Image, Picture, Media, ShoeImage, ProductImage) with only plain attributes before it. New text: letters, digits, spaces and . , : ; ' & | ( ) / ? - and en dash (accented Latin letters on standard sites, printable ASCII only on health sites); no backslash, angle bracket, brace, $, backtick, = or entity; titles and headings up to 120 characters, descriptions 320, alt 200. health: true also holds any heading, frontmatter title or h1, alt text, body rewording, and any added value with a price, offer, percentage, dose, drug or injectable brand name or claim word. Schema and JSON-LD, SEO and metadata helpers, sitemaps, robots, llms files, image lists and every other .ts, .js, .json or .txt file now wait for Arsany. protectedPaths: lowercase path segments never linked from an added line, on top of the built-in start, lp, intake, quiz, checkout, cart, portal, login, account, booking, check-in, admin and api; link targets are decoded and their dot segments, duplicate slashes and backslashes resolved first. metaObjects: [{files, parents}]: .ts files whose title and description keys may be reworded when the unchanged lines above them by indentation match parents (anchored, nearest first). blog branches: only new Markdown posts under futureDate files (date a plain YYYY-MM-DD after today in Los Angeles) and binaryOk images. frontmatter: {dir, ext, keys, nested, linkKeys, slugKey, components}: a new post sits directly in dir with a lowercase name and a slug no existing post has, sets only listed keys (never canonical, permalink, redirect, layout), has no backslash and nothing that folds to an angle bracket in its frontmatter, keeps URLs relative or on hosts (linkKeys may link out over https), and its body has no raw HTML (only listed components with plain string attributes), no import or export line, no braces in MDX and no image from outside hosts. denyPatch: regular expressions (case-insensitive), or {pattern, files}; a changed line matching one holds. denySquashed: lowercase words held when they appear in a changed line with everything but letters and digits removed. hosts: the only URL hosts a changed line may name. An unknown key (linkOnly, linkOnlyIgnore, lineOk, dataFiles and altText are no longer known) or a rule file that does not parse holds every pull request. Set enabled to false to hold every pull request of that kind.
